title: Feedback lifecycle & API core: append-only correction pattern
executive_summary: The database/chairman-gated/20260907_feedback_immutability_trigger.sql migration made public.feedback append-only (UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE all rejected via BEFORE ENABLE ALWAYS triggers).

functional_requirements.title: Shared feedback-correction helper module
functional_requirements.description: New lib/governance/feedback-correction.js exports rootIdOf(row) (resolves metadata.corrects_feedback_id or row.id -- ALWAYS the root of the chain, never the immediately-prior row, so a single lookup finds the current state with no multi-hop chain-walking), buildFeedbackCorrection(existingRow, changes) (returns an INSERT payload: drops id/created_at, ALWAYS nulls error_hash and strips metadata.dedup_hash from the copied metadata to avoid colliding with the three live partial UNIQUE indexes on public.feedback keyed on those fields -- idx_feedback_venture_error_hash, idx_feedback_error_capture_hash, idx_feedback_telemetry_dedup -- applies changes, sets metadata.corrects_feedback_id=rootId and preserves metadata.original_created_at, sets a fresh updated_at), and fetchLatestFeedback(supabase, feedbackId) (resolves any id in a correction chain to its current row via a base fetch + a root-scoped .or('id.eq.ROOT,metadata->>corrects_feedback_id.eq.ROOT').order('created_at', {ascending:false}).order('id', {ascending:false}).limit(1) query -- the secondary order('id', desc) is a DETERMINISTIC tie-break, not a recency claim: two corrections can share a created_at timestamp, and without a fixed secondary key the same query could return a different row on repeated calls, silently breaking the idempotency guards in FR-2/FR-6 (adversarial LEAD-phase critique finding, warn-severity). fetchLatestFeedback's own DB-error path returns {error} explicitly and every caller MUST treat that as fail-closed -- refuse to write / surface an error -- NEVER silently fall back to trusting the raw root row as if it were current (an INV-001-class control-without-could-not-check-path gap the same critique flagged); this fail-closed contract is itself covered by a test (TS-26).
acceptance_criteria: rootIdOf never returns an intermediate correction's id for a 2+-hop chain (TS-3)
buildFeedbackCorrection never reproduces error_hash or metadata.dedup_hash on the correction payload (TS-5)
fetchLatestFeedback resolves a mid-chain id to the newest row in the chain (TS-7)
Two corrections sharing an identical created_at timestamp resolve deterministically via the id-desc tie-break, same result on every call (TS-25)
A fetchLatestFeedback DB error is surfaced to the caller and never silently treated as 'root row is current' (TS-26)

functional_requirements.title: server/routes/feedback.js: POST /:id/promote-to-sd and PATCH /:id/status converted to insert-correction
functional_requirements.description: Both live HTTP routes fetch the feedback row, resolve it to its LATEST correction via fetchLatestFeedback (never trust the raw .eq('id',id) row for status/idempotency decisions), then insert a correction via buildFeedbackCorrection instead of calling .update(). promote-to-sd's `if (feedback.resolution_sd_id)` idempotency guard reads the resolved latest row so a second click never mints a second strategic_directives_v2 row; a failed correction-insert now returns an error response instead of silently warn-and-succeed (closing a pre-existing duplicate-SD-mint bug the current warn-only path already has). PATCH /:id/status's FR-4 validateStatusTransition call is evaluated against the resolved latest row, not the stale root. Also fixes an incidental dead gate at L58 (feedback.quality_score does not exist on the table -- the real columns are rubric_score/quality_assessment -- so the quality gate has always been a no-op; corrected to read rubric_score, in the same file already being touched).
acceptance_criteria: Two sequential POST /:id/promote-to-sd calls mint exactly one SD row (TS-11)
PATCH /:id/status validates transitions against current, not stale, state (TS-13)
Neither route issues a .from('feedback').update(...) call

functional_requirements.title: scripts/feedback-staleness-check.js converted to insert-correction, never writes status='stale'
functional_requirements.description: LEAD validation-agent confirmed 'stale' is not a member of the live feedback_status_check CHECK constraint (allowed: new, triaged, in_progress, resolved, wont_fix, duplicate, invalid, backlog, shipped) -- the ORIGINAL update() would fail on this constraint independent of the append-only trigger. Fix: the bulk scan is root-scoped (.is('metadata->>corrects_feedback_id', null)) so correction rows are never re-selected as fresh staleness candidates; for each candidate root, fetchLatestFeedback resolves current state and the script skips it if already marked stale (metadata.marked_stale_at present) or already moved off status new/triaged by another path. Otherwise it inserts a correction that leaves `status` UNCHANGED and records staleness via metadata.marked_stale_at + the existing resolution_notes message. Chunked at the existing UPDATE_CHUNK=200 convention.
acceptance_criteria: No write ever sets status='stale' (would violate feedback_status_check)

Running the script twice over the same fixture root inserts zero rows on the second run (TS-15) -- the highest-risk regression class: without this it inserts one correction per candidate on every cron run forever
Root-only scan predicate is present and tested (TS-18)

functional_requirements.title: scripts/feedback-link-resolution.mjs converted to insert-correction (both write branches)
functional_requirements.description: Widen the initial select from 'id, status' to '*' (needed to build a full correction payload). Both the resolveFeedback()-delegating branch (already covered by FR-6) and the direct link-only .update() in the else branch (setting resolution_sd_id or quick_fix_id) are converted to insert a correction via the shared helper, resolved against fetchLatestFeedback first.
acceptance_criteria: Both write branches (resolve path and link-only path) use insert-correction, not .update() (TS-17)

functional_requirements.title: scripts/feedback-age-out.mjs converted to insert-correction (adds the per-row fetch it currently lacks)
functional_requirements.description: The current implementation is a pure set-based bulk UPDATE with no per-row fetch at all. Fix: first SELECT the full matching root rows (category='informational_note', archived_at IS NULL, updated_at < cutoff, metadata->>corrects_feedback_id IS NULL), chunked; for each, resolve latest via fetchLatestFeedback and skip if already archived by another correction; otherwise insert a correction setting archived_at=now(). No live candidates exist today (0 rows), so this is a forward-looking, latent-defect fix verified via a seeded fixture, not observed production behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic 2-row fixture: first run archives both via correction, second run inserts zero new rows (TS-16)
Root-only scan predicate present

functional_requirements.title: lib/governance/resolve-feedback.js: resolveFeedback() converted to insert-correction, backward-compatible return contract
functional_requirements.description: The canonical resolver (7 live callers) resolves the input feedbackId to its LATEST correction via fetchLatestFeedback; if the latest row's status is already 'resolved', returns the EXACT existing shape {updated:false, id:feedbackId, reason:'no_row_or_already_resolved'} unchanged (a LEAD risk-agent audit found 3 production callers -- complete-quick-fix/orchestrator.js, reconcile-feedback-references.js, apply-chairman-decision-captures.mjs -- compare this exact string with strict equality; changing it silently routes an already-resolved outcome into their failure branch). Otherwise inserts a correction with status='resolved', resolved_at=now(), and the optional quick_fix_id/resolution_sd_id/resolution_notes/resolution_type fields, and returns {updated:true, id:feedbackId} (the returned id stays the ORIGINAL input id for full backward compatibility -- no caller reads a 'new row id' field, confirmed by the same audit, so none is added).
acceptance_criteria: resolveFeedback() never calls .update() on feedback (TS-9)
Calling it twice against an already-resolved chain returns the pinned reason string on the second call with no second INSERT (TS-10)
The reason string 'no_row_or_already_resolved' is byte-identical to the pre-existing value

functional_requirements.title: New dedicated table withheld_promotion_markers replaces feedback.metadata bookkeeping for 2 pipeline sites
functional_requirements.description: lib/governance/withheld-registry.mjs (writeMarkers/readPendingMarkers/consumeMarker/disposeMarker) and scripts/feedback-fingerprint-promoter.mjs's own promoted_to_qf metadata-merge site stop reading/writing feedback.metadata entirely for this bookkeeping (a LEAD risk-agent review measured the insert-correction alternative would add ~440 rows/day of pure bookkeeping churn against a ~132/day organic baseline, a +333% write-volume increase, AND found a hard architectural blocker: feedback-fingerprint-promoter.mjs's existing server-side PostgREST .or() predicate for 'pending marker not yet promoted/disposed' cannot be re-expressed as 'the latest correction in a chain', a defect class the file's own history already documents once). The new table (feedback_id PK/FK to feedback.id, fingerprint, member_feedback_ids uuid[], max_severity, admission_path, gauge_value, floor, engine, decision, first_withheld_at/run, last_withheld_at/run, withheld_run_count, promoted_at/qf_id/fingerprint, disposed_by/reason/at, created_at, updated_at) carries NO append-only trigger -- ordinary UPDATE is legal there -- and is confirmed TIER-1 (worker-auto-appliable via scripts/apply-migration.js, no chairman ceremony) by scripts/lib/migration-tier-classifier.mjs, PROVIDED the migration contains no ON DELETE CASCADE, no DO $verify$ block, and no COMMENT ON containing a forbidden verb (all three would flip it TIER-2 per a LEAD testing-agent probe) -- so behavioural verification is a separate db-tier vitest test (TS-19), never an inline DO block. RLS: the table is written/read exclusively by the SAME server-role Supabase client withheld-registry.mjs and feedback-fingerprint-promoter.mjs already construct today (SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, which bypasses RLS entirely -- rolbypassrls=true, identical to every other governance table these two files touch); RLS is enabled with a single permissive service-role policy (mirrors the pattern already used elsewhere in lib/governance), and TS-27 proves the actual client construction these two files use can select/insert/update the new table end-to-end, not merely that a policy exists on paper (adversarial LEAD-phase critique finding, warn-severity: 'under-specified RLS can cause late integration failures').
acceptance_criteria: database/migrations/<ts>_withheld_promotion_markers.sql classifies TIER-1 via classifyMigration() before merge
withheld-registry.mjs and feedback-fingerprint-promoter.mjs contain zero .from('feedback').update( calls for marker bookkeeping (TS-22)
Ordinary UPDATE against the new table succeeds (no trigger) (TS-19)
The exact service-role client construction used by both producer files can select/insert/update the new table (TS-27)

functional_requirements.title: Backfill existing feedback.metadata markers into withheld_promotion_markers, with a before/after count gate
functional_requirements.description: A LEAD testing-agent audit measured 136 live rows carrying metadata.withheld_pending (110 still pending) and 117 carrying metadata.promoted_to_qf. Shipping the new table with no backfill would silently drop every pending marker -- reproducing the exact silent-expiry defect withheld-registry.mjs's own module docstring says it was written to abolish. A one-off backfill script (scripts/one-off/backfill-withheld-promotion-markers.mjs) migrates every existing marker (both withheld_pending and promoted_to_qf) into the new table. Per an adversarial LEAD-phase critique finding (INV-002-repair-gated-on-code-present-not-data-present: 'a seeder/backfill ships with no acceptance criterion measuring the DATA it produces'), the backfill is NOT considered done on 'script ran without error' -- it prints and the EXEC evidence records an explicit before-count (measured from feedback.metadata) vs. after-count (measured from withheld_promotion_markers) comparison, and FR-9's cutover gate refuses to proceed unless those counts match.
acceptance_criteria: Post-backfill readPendingMarkers() (rewired to the new table) returns the same pending set (by feedback_id) as the pre-backfill feedback.metadata scan returned (TS-21)
All 117 promoted_to_qf markers land in the new table's promoted_at/promoted_fingerprint columns
The backfill script's own output states the before-count and after-count explicitly (TS-28)

functional_requirements.title: Reversible cutover for withheld_promotion_markers: verified-backfill gate + revert path
functional_requirements.description: Directly closes the adversarial LEAD-phase critique's sole BLOCK finding: 'the plan provides no rollback/safety procedure if the backfill is wrong or the rewire causes dropped/duplicated markers in production... not trivially reversible once new writes start landing.' Sequencing (each step is a precondition for the next, not parallelizable): (1) apply the withheld_promotion_markers migration -- purely additive, does not touch feedback or existing producer behavior, safe on its own; (2) run the backfill script and verify its before/after counts match (FR-8) BEFORE any producer code changes ship -- at this point the new table is fully populated but nothing reads or writes it yet, so a bad backfill is trivially fixed by re-running it with zero production impact; (3) ONLY after the count-match gate passes, cut withheld-registry.mjs and feedback-fingerprint-promoter.mjs over to read/write the new table exclusively. Rollback if the cutover (step 3) misbehaves: git-revert the producer-file changes (step 1's migration and step 2's backfilled data are NOT reverted -- they are purely additive and harmless to leave in place); the reverted producer code resumes reading/writing feedback.metadata exactly as it did before this SD, which still holds the pre-cutover marker state untouched (this SD's design never deletes or mutates the legacy feedback.metadata markers -- it only stops writing new ones there), so a revert is a clean, zero-data-loss return to the pre-SD behavior. There is deliberately no dual-read/dual-write window: the critique's suggested alternative (feature-flagged dual-read) was rejected because it would require the SAME non-terminating-write hazard analysis (FR-1) applied to TWO code paths simultaneously for the marker-bookkeeping case that FR-7 exists specifically to avoid; a clean verified-then-atomic cutover with a pure-revert rollback is simpler and equally safe given step 2's pre-cutover verification gate.
acceptance_criteria: The migration (step 1) and backfill (step 2) are committed and verified in a state where zero producer code has changed yet
Producer cutover (step 3) only proceeds once FR-8's count-match gate passes
A revert of the producer-file commit alone (without touching the migration/backfill commits) restores pre-SD behavior with no data loss

technical_requirements.title: No UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE against public.feedback anywhere in the 7 owned files
technical_requirements.description: The append-only trigger (feedback_no_update/feedback_no_delete_trg/feedback_no_truncate_trg, all ENABLE ALWAYS) is out of scope to modify -- it is a chairman-ratified, cross-cutting invariant (SD-LEO-ORCH-CAPA-DURABILITY-AUDIT-001-E). Every write in scope is an INSERT.

technical_requirements.title: Correction inserts must not collide with live partial UNIQUE indexes
technical_requirements.description: idx_feedback_venture_error_hash (venture_id, error_hash) WHERE feedback_type='venture_error' AND venture_id IS NOT NULL; idx_feedback_error_capture_hash (error_hash) WHERE source_type='error_capture' AND feedback_type='sentry_error' AND venture_id IS NULL; idx_feedback_telemetry_dedup (category, metadata->>'dedup_hash') WHERE category='fleet_dormancy'. buildFeedbackCorrection nulls error_hash and strips metadata.dedup_hash unconditionally (NULL is never equal to NULL under a unique index, so this structurally avoids all three without per-index special-casing).

technical_requirements.title: New table migration must stay TIER-1
technical_requirements.description: No ON DELETE CASCADE on the feedback_id FK, no DO $verify$ block, no COMMENT ON containing a forbidden verb (UPDATE/DELETE/GRANT/etc). classifyMigration() from scripts/lib/migration-tier-classifier.mjs must return tier:1 before the migration is applied via scripts/apply-migration.js.

technical_requirements.title: Backward-compatible resolveFeedback() contract
technical_requirements.description: resolveFeedback()'s returned shape ({updated, id, reason, error}) is unchanged in field names and in the exact string 'no_row_or_already_resolved'. No new required field is added that existing callers must adopt.

technical_requirements.title: No DB-tier test may leave permanent residue on public.feedback
technical_requirements.description: feedback rows can never be deleted (append-only + no DELETE). All feedback-table interactions in this SD's tests use vi.mock('@supabase/supabase-js') (unit tier, no DB). The withheld_promotion_markers table has no such constraint, so its db-tier tests (tests/*.db.test.js via describeDb/itDb) may freely insert/update/delete fixture rows there.

technical_requirements.title: Deterministic latest-row resolution
technical_requirements.description: fetchLatestFeedback orders by created_at DESC, id DESC (a fixed, deterministic secondary key -- not a recency claim, purely a tie-break so the same query always returns the same row). Any DB error from this resolution is returned to the caller explicitly and MUST be treated as fail-closed by every call site (refuse to write / surface an error) -- never silently treated as 'the root row is current'.

technical_requirements.title: withheld_promotion_markers access is service-role only, matching existing producer clients
technical_requirements.description: No new role or credential is introduced. RLS is enabled with a permissive service-role policy; the table is reachable only via the SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY client withheld-registry.mjs and feedback-fingerprint-promoter.mjs already construct (rolbypassrls=true), identical to how these two files already reach every other table they touch.

plan_checklist.text: SD requirements mapped to technical specs

risks.risk: A converted site's read-before-write guard resolves against the stale root instead of the latest correction, making the site non-terminating (re-fires every run/request forever)
risks.mitigation: Every read-before-write decision routes through fetchLatestFeedback or an explicit root-scoped scan; TS-10/TS-11/TS-15/TS-16 each assert termination on a second run/request.

risks.risk: Correction insert collides with a live partial UNIQUE index on public.feedback (venture_error/error_capture error_hash, fleet_dormancy dedup_hash)
risks.mitigation: buildFeedbackCorrection unconditionally nulls error_hash and strips metadata.dedup_hash; TS-5 pins this.

risks.risk: The new withheld_promotion_markers migration drifts to TIER-2 (chairman-gated) if a future edit adds ON DELETE CASCADE, a DO block, or a destructive-verb COMMENT
risks.mitigation: TR-3 states the constraint explicitly; classifyMigration() is run and its tier:1 verdict checked before apply.

risks.risk: Backfill omits or duplicates existing withheld/promoted markers
risks.mitigation: TS-21 compares the pending set before and after backfill by feedback_id; TS-28 pins an explicit before/after count report; FR-9's cutover gate refuses producer changes until counts match.

risks.risk: The withheld_promotion_markers migration + backfill + producer cutover is a persistent-side-effect change with no stated rollback (adversarial LEAD-phase critique BLOCK finding)
risks.mitigation: FR-9 sequences migration -> verified backfill -> producer cutover as three independently-committable steps; migration and backfill are purely additive and safe standalone; rollback of the cutover is a plain git-revert of the producer-file commit, restoring feedback.metadata reads/writes with the legacy markers still intact (never deleted).

risks.risk: Two correction rows for the same root share an identical created_at timestamp, making 'latest' nondeterministic across repeated fetchLatestFeedback calls and silently breaking an idempotency guard

content:
# Product Requirements Document

## Strategic Directive
SD-LEO-INFRA-AUDIT-FIX-FEEDBACK-001-A

## Title
Feedback lifecycle & API core: fix 7 feedback.update() call sites broken by the append-only trigger

## Status
Planning

## Executive Summary
The database/chairman-gated/20260907_feedback_immutability_trigger.sql migration made public.feedback append-only (UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE all rejected via BEFORE ENABLE ALWAYS triggers). This child of the parent audit orchestrator delivers TWO coupled changes, both required to close the defect: (1) a shared insert-a-correction-row helper (lib/governance/feedback-correction.js, precedent: QF-20260911-515's gauge-runner fix) applied to the 5 lifecycle-writer call sites this child owns across server/routes/feedback.js, feedback-staleness-check.js, feedback-link-resolution.mjs, feedback-age-out.mjs, and resolve-feedback.js; and (2) a genuinely dedicated, freely-mutable side table (withheld_promotion_markers, TIER-1 auto-appliable, no chairman ceremony) plus a verified backfill and a reversible cutover, replacing feedback.metadata bookkeeping in the 2 remaining owned sites (feedback-fingerprint-promoter.mjs, withheld-registry.mjs, 3 write sites) that a LEAD risk-agent review confirmed cannot safely share the append-only, insert-only model without unbounded row growth and a server-side query that cannot express 'latest correction wins'. This is explicitly NOT a narrow 7-call-site patch: FR-7/FR-8/FR-9 constitute a small, independent data-model change (new table, backfill, and a producer cutover with a defined rollback path) and are called out as such rather than folded silently into 'fixing an update() call'. Every converted read-before-write site is re-pointed to resolve against the LATEST correction in a chain (never the stale root row) via a deterministic tie-break, closing a non-termination class of regression a risk-agent review surfaced: without this, every converted site would re-fire on every subsequent run/request forever.

## Functional Requirements

### FR-1: undefined
New lib/governance/feedback-correction.js exports rootIdOf(row) (resolves metadata.corrects_feedback_id or row.id -- ALWAYS the root of the chain, never the immediately-prior row, so a single lookup finds the current state with no multi-hop chain-walking), buildFeedbackCorrection(existingRow, changes) (returns an INSERT payload: drops id/created_at, ALWAYS nulls error_hash and strips metadata.dedup_hash from the copied metadata to avoid colliding with the three live partial UNIQUE indexes on public.feedback keyed on those fields -- idx_feedback_venture_error_hash, idx_feedback_error_capture_hash, idx_feedback_telemetry_dedup -- applies changes, sets metadata.corrects_feedback_id=rootId and preserves metadata.original_created_at, sets a fresh updated_at), and fetchLatestFeedback(supabase, feedbackId) (resolves any id in a correction chain to its current row via a base fetch + a root-scoped .or('id.eq.ROOT,metadata->>corrects_feedback_id.eq.ROOT').order('created_at', {ascending:false}).order('id', {ascending:false}).limit(1) query -- the secondary order('id', desc) is a DETERMINISTIC tie-break, not a recency claim: two corrections can share a created_at timestamp, and without a fixed secondary key the same query could return a different row on repeated calls, silently breaking the idempotency guards in FR-2/FR-6 (adversarial LEAD-phase critique finding, warn-severity). fetchLatestFeedback's own DB-error path returns {error} explicitly and every caller MUST treat that as fail-closed -- refuse to write / surface an error -- NEVER silently fall back to trusting the raw root row as if it were current (an INV-001-class control-without-could-not-check-path gap the same critique flagged); this fail-closed contract is itself covered by a test (TS-26).
**Priority**: critical
**Acceptance Criteria**:- rootIdOf never returns an intermediate correction's id for a 2+-hop chain (TS-3)- buildFeedbackCorrection never reproduces error_hash or metadata.dedup_hash on the correction payload (TS-5)- fetchLatestFeedback resolves a mid-chain id to the newest row in the chain (TS-7)- Two corrections sharing an identical created_at timestamp resolve deterministically via the id-desc tie-break, same result on every call (TS-25)- A fetchLatestFeedback DB error is surfaced to the caller and never silently treated as 'root row is current' (TS-26)

### FR-2: undefined
Both live HTTP routes fetch the feedback row, resolve it to its LATEST correction via fetchLatestFeedback (never trust the raw .eq('id',id) row for status/idempotency decisions), then insert a correction via buildFeedbackCorrection instead of calling .update(). promote-to-sd's `if (feedback.resolution_sd_id)` idempotency guard reads the resolved latest row so a second click never mints a second strategic_directives_v2 row; a failed correction-insert now returns an error response instead of silently warn-and-succeed (closing a pre-existing duplicate-SD-mint bug the current warn-only path already has). PATCH /:id/status's FR-4 validateStatusTransition call is evaluated against the resolved latest row, not the stale root. Also fixes an incidental dead gate at L58 (feedback.quality_score does not exist on the table -- the real columns are rubric_score/quality_assessment -- so the quality gate has always been a no-op; corrected to read rubric_score, in the same file already being touched).
**Priority**: critical
**Acceptance Criteria**:- Two sequential POST /:id/promote-to-sd calls mint exactly one SD row (TS-11)- PATCH /:id/status validates transitions against current, not stale, state (TS-13)- Neither route issues a .from('feedback').update(...) call

### FR-3: undefined
LEAD validation-agent confirmed 'stale' is not a member of the live feedback_status_check CHECK constraint (allowed: new, triaged, in_progress, resolved, wont_fix, duplicate, invalid, backlog, shipped) -- the ORIGINAL update() would fail on this constraint independent of the append-only trigger. Fix: the bulk scan is root-scoped (.is('metadata->>corrects_feedback_id', null)) so correction rows are never re-selected as fresh staleness candidates; for each candidate root, fetchLatestFeedback resolves current state and the script skips it if already marked stale (metadata.marked_stale_at present) or already moved off status new/triaged by another path. Otherwise it inserts a correction that leaves `status` UNCHANGED and records staleness via metadata.marked_stale_at + the existing resolution_notes message. Chunked at the existing UPDATE_CHUNK=200 convention.
**Priority**: critical
**Acceptance Criteria**:- No write ever sets status='stale' (would violate feedback_status_check)- Running the script twice over the same fixture root inserts zero rows on the second run (TS-15) -- the highest-risk regression class: without this it inserts one correction per candidate on every cron run forever- Root-only scan predicate is present and tested (TS-18)

### FR-4: undefined
Widen the initial select from 'id, status' to '*' (needed to build a full correction payload). Both the resolveFeedback()-delegating branch (already covered by FR-6) and the direct link-only .update() in the else branch (setting resolution_sd_id or quick_fix_id) are converted to insert a correction via the shared helper, resolved against fetchLatestFeedback first.
**Priority**: high
**Acceptance Criteria**:- Both write branches (resolve path and link-only path) use insert-correction, not .update() (TS-17)

### FR-5: undefined
The current implementation is a pure set-based bulk UPDATE with no per-row fetch at all. Fix: first SELECT the full matching root rows (category='informational_note', archived_at IS NULL, updated_at < cutoff, metadata->>corrects_feedback_id IS NULL), chunked; for each, resolve latest via fetchLatestFeedback and skip if already archived by another correction; otherwise insert a correction setting archived_at=now(). No live candidates exist today (0 rows), so this is a forward-looking, latent-defect fix verified via a seeded fixture, not observed production behavior.
**Priority**: medium
**Acceptance Criteria**:- A synthetic 2-row fixture: first run archives both via correction, second run inserts zero new rows (TS-16)- Root-only scan predicate present

### FR-6: undefined
The canonical resolver (7 live callers) resolves the input feedbackId to its LATEST correction via fetchLatestFeedback; if the latest row's status is already 'resolved', returns the EXACT existing shape {updated:false, id:feedbackId, reason:'no_row_or_already_resolved'} unchanged (a LEAD risk-agent audit found 3 production callers -- complete-quick-fix/orchestrator.js, reconcile-feedback-references.js, apply-chairman-decision-captures.mjs -- compare this exact string with strict equality; changing it silently routes an already-resolved outcome into their failure branch). Otherwise inserts a correction with status='resolved', resolved_at=now(), and the optional quick_fix_id/resolution_sd_id/resolution_notes/resolution_type fields, and returns {updated:true, id:feedbackId} (the returned id stays the ORIGINAL input id for full backward compatibility -- no caller reads a 'new row id' field, confirmed by the same audit, so none is added).
**Priority**: critical
**Acceptance Criteria**:- resolveFeedback() never calls .update() on feedback (TS-9)- Calling it twice against an already-resolved chain returns the pinned reason string on the second call with no second INSERT (TS-10)- The reason string 'no_row_or_already_resolved' is byte-identical to the pre-existing value

### FR-7: undefined
lib/governance/withheld-registry.mjs (writeMarkers/readPendingMarkers/consumeMarker/disposeMarker) and scripts/feedback-fingerprint-promoter.mjs's own promoted_to_qf metadata-merge site stop reading/writing feedback.metadata entirely for this bookkeeping (a LEAD risk-agent review measured the insert-correction alternative would add ~440 rows/day of pure bookkeeping churn against a ~132/day organic baseline, a +333% write-volume increase, AND found a hard architectural blocker: feedback-fingerprint-promoter.mjs's existing server-side PostgREST .or() predicate for 'pending marker not yet promoted/disposed' cannot be re-expressed as 'the latest correction in a chain', a defect class the file's own history already documents once). The new table (feedback_id PK/FK to feedback.id, fingerprint, member_feedback_ids uuid[], max_severity, admission_path, gauge_value, floor, engine, decision, first_withheld_at/run, last_withheld_at/run, withheld_run_count, promoted_at/qf_id/fingerprint, disposed_by/reason/at, created_at, updated_at) carries NO append-only trigger -- ordinary UPDATE is legal there -- and is confirmed TIER-1 (worker-auto-appliable via scripts/apply-migration.js, no chairman ceremony) by scripts/lib/migration-tier-classifier.mjs, PROVIDED the migration contains no ON DELETE CASCADE, no DO $verify$ block, and no COMMENT ON containing a forbidden verb (all three would flip it TIER-2 per a LEAD testing-agent probe) -- so behavioural verification is a separate db-tier vitest test (TS-19), never an inline DO block. RLS: the table is written/read exclusively by the SAME server-role Supabase client withheld-registry.mjs and feedback-fingerprint-promoter.mjs already construct today (SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, which bypasses RLS entirely -- rolbypassrls=true, identical to every other governance table these two files touch); RLS is enabled with a single permissive service-role policy (mirrors the pattern already used elsewhere in lib/governance), and TS-27 proves the actual client construction these two files use can select/insert/update the new table end-to-end, not merely that a policy exists on paper (adversarial LEAD-phase critique finding, warn-severity: 'under-specified RLS can cause late integration failures').
**Priority**: critical
**Acceptance Criteria**:- database/migrations/<ts>_withheld_promotion_markers.sql classifies TIER-1 via classifyMigration() before merge- withheld-registry.mjs and feedback-fingerprint-promoter.mjs contain zero .from('feedback').update( calls for marker bookkeeping (TS-22)- Ordinary UPDATE against the new table succeeds (no trigger) (TS-19)- The exact service-role client construction used by both producer files can select/insert/update the new table (TS-27)

### FR-8: undefined
A LEAD testing-agent audit measured 136 live rows carrying metadata.withheld_pending (110 still pending) and 117 carrying metadata.promoted_to_qf. Shipping the new table with no backfill would silently drop every pending marker -- reproducing the exact silent-expiry defect withheld-registry.mjs's own module docstring says it was written to abolish. A one-off backfill script (scripts/one-off/backfill-withheld-promotion-markers.mjs) migrates every existing marker (both withheld_pending and promoted_to_qf) into the new table. Per an adversarial LEAD-phase critique finding (INV-002-repair-gated-on-code-present-not-data-present: 'a seeder/backfill ships with no acceptance criterion measuring the DATA it produces'), the backfill is NOT considered done on 'script ran without error' -- it prints and the EXEC evidence records an explicit before-count (measured from feedback.metadata) vs. after-count (measured from withheld_promotion_markers) comparison, and FR-9's cutover gate refuses to proceed unless those counts match.
**Priority**: critical
**Acceptance Criteria**:- Post-backfill readPendingMarkers() (rewired to the new table) returns the same pending set (by feedback_id) as the pre-backfill feedback.metadata scan returned (TS-21)- All 117 promoted_to_qf markers land in the new table's promoted_at/promoted_fingerprint columns- The backfill script's own output states the before-count and after-count explicitly (TS-28)

### FR-9: undefined
Directly closes the adversarial LEAD-phase critique's sole BLOCK finding: 'the plan provides no rollback/safety procedure if the backfill is wrong or the rewire causes dropped/duplicated markers in production... not trivially reversible once new writes start landing.' Sequencing (each step is a precondition for the next, not parallelizable): (1) apply the withheld_promotion_markers migration -- purely additive, does not touch feedback or existing producer behavior, safe on its own; (2) run the backfill script and verify its before/after counts match (FR-8) BEFORE any producer code changes ship -- at this point the new table is fully populated but nothing reads or writes it yet, so a bad backfill is trivially fixed by re-running it with zero production impact; (3) ONLY after the count-match gate passes, cut withheld-registry.mjs and feedback-fingerprint-promoter.mjs over to read/write the new table exclusively. Rollback if the cutover (step 3) misbehaves: git-revert the producer-file changes (step 1's migration and step 2's backfilled data are NOT reverted -- they are purely additive and harmless to leave in place); the reverted producer code resumes reading/writing feedback.metadata exactly as it did before this SD, which still holds the pre-cutover marker state untouched (this SD's design never deletes or mutates the legacy feedback.metadata markers -- it only stops writing new ones there), so a revert is a clean, zero-data-loss return to the pre-SD behavior. There is deliberately no dual-read/dual-write window: the critique's suggested alternative (feature-flagged dual-read) was rejected because it would require the SAME non-terminating-write hazard analysis (FR-1) applied to TWO code paths simultaneously for the marker-bookkeeping case that FR-7 exists specifically to avoid; a clean verified-then-atomic cutover with a pure-revert rollback is simpler and equally safe given step 2's pre-cutover verification gate.
**Priority**: critical
**Acceptance Criteria**:- The migration (step 1) and backfill (step 2) are committed and verified in a state where zero producer code has changed yet- Producer cutover (step 3) only proceeds once FR-8's count-match gate passes- A revert of the producer-file commit alone (without touching the migration/backfill commits) restores pre-SD behavior with no data loss
